title: Flame Design: a novel approach to clean, efficient diffusion flames
study: Soot-inception and extinction limits of spherical and coflow diffusion flames of ethylene and methane, across flow rate, inert gas and pressure.
earthRelevance: Aims at more efficient, lower-emission combustors on Earth; the record cites input to future coal power plant designs.

title: Burning Rate Emulator
study: Gas burners that imitate burning solids and liquids, tested in still air at spacecraft atmospheres from 21% to 34% oxygen.
earthRelevance: Preliminary: flames kept burning with no airflow in oxygen-enriched atmospheres, while those at 21% oxygen went out quickly. Supports wider use of cone-calorimeter material testing.

title: Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame
study: Weak and heavily sooting coflow flames of methane and ethylene: shape, lift-off, temperature, soot and extinction, as benchmark data for models.
earthRelevance: Diffusion flames are the type in most practical devices. Better prediction of soot, radiation and extinction helps fire suppression and engine efficiency.

title: Electric-field effects on laminar diffusion flames
study: How an electric field changes ion current, flame stability and soot in laminar diffusion flames.
earthRelevance: Electric-field control could cut pollutants and fuel use in terrestrial combustion. The record says it serves no direct space application.

title: Structure and response of spherical diffusion flames
study: Transient structure and extinction limits of spherical flames, soot-free and sooty, compared with detailed simulation.
earthRelevance: Diffusion flames underlie many engines and devices; cleaner data improves prediction of power, efficiency, emissions and reliability.

title: Burning and Suppression of Solids II
study: Ignition, flame growth, spread and extinction limits of thicker solid fuels in slow forced airflow, and how they relate to the 1 g material test.
earthRelevance: Evaluates fuel-burning models that can then be used on Earth for wildfires, building fires and energy recovery from waste.

title: Burning and Suppression of Solids
study: Solid fuels in realistic shapes, including wake flames, and how well nitrogen puts them out.
earthRelevance: Models validated in the simple microgravity flow are then built up to capture flames in normal gravity, with wide use across terrestrial combustion problems.

title: Cool Flames Investigation
study: Droplets of n-dodecane and blends at 0.25 to 5 atm: cool-flame behaviour, helium dilution, extinction and soot.
earthRelevance: Cool flames matter for ignition of practical fuels, HCCI engine design, and how octane and cetane ratings arise.

title: Computational and experimental analysis of SPICE data sets
study: Re-analysis of over 1,600 SPICE flame images with soot modelling, to explain why soot differs so much between 1 g and 0 g.
earthRelevance: Better soot and radiation models for cleaner energy and industrial systems.

title: Concurrent flame spread modelling with flamelet generated manifolds, compared with BASS
study: A new modelling method for flame spread along a solid in the direction of airflow, checked against BASS measurements.
earthRelevance: Predictive screening of material flammability limits; the record says it could improve fire modelling and safety standards on Earth.

title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment 2
study: Two-component fuel droplets under conditions closer to real combustors: mixing, extinction and benchmark data for simulation.
earthRelevance: Liquid fuels power transport. The data supports surrogate fuels and validation of jet-engine combustion models.

title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
study: Flammability limits of burning liquid droplets and the effect of the suppressants CO2, helium and SF6.
earthRelevance: Informs suppression in confined settings such as submarines and high-altitude aircraft; its cool-flame findings feed engine design.

title: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment I
study: How fast a large fire grows in low gravity, and how low-gravity flammability limits compare with the 1 g screening test.
earthRelevance: Fire in a small sealed vehicle is a stand-in for mines, aircraft and submarines.

title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment II
study: Large-scale fire growth and flammability limits for several spacecraft materials in low gravity.
earthRelevance: Same Earth link as Saffire-I: fire safety in sealed spaces such as mines, aircraft and submarines.

title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment III
study: Large-scale fire growth in low gravity, continuing the Saffire series.
earthRelevance: Same Earth link as Saffire-I: fire safety in sealed spaces such as mines, aircraft and submarines.

title: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment, reflight
study: Sizes of smoke particles from overheated materials in low gravity, repeated after sample contamination in the first run.
earthRelevance: Better detectors for extreme environments on Earth such as submarines and underwater laboratories.

title: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment
study: Smoke droplet size in low gravity, linked to how the smoke was made and carried, with a growth model.
earthRelevance: Baseline data for judging smoke detectors; useful for submarines and underwater laboratories.

title: Structure and Liftoff in Combustion Experiment
study: Structure and stability of laminar diffusion flames: lift-off limits, nitrogen dilution, soot and radiative loss.
earthRelevance: Better numerical models for efficient combustion, low-emission systems and cleaner engines and industrial burners.

title: Smoke Point in Co-flow Experiment
study: The smoke point of non-buoyant jet flames: how burner size, coflow speed and fuel change the flame length at which soot escapes.
earthRelevance: Better soot models; the record says it could inform fuel formulation and combustion processes.

title: Surface Tension Driven Convection Experiment 1
study: Flows driven by surface tension in a heated liquid. A fluid physics experiment, not a flame study.
earthRelevance: Its infrared imaging and particle velocimetry methods are now used to study combustion and other flows on Earth.

title: Using SAME data for simulation of smoke generation in microgravity
study: Simulation of how gravity changes smoke particle growth from overheated materials.
earthRelevance: Tools that predict smoke character from temperature, gravity and material, leading to better smoke detectors.

title: Effect of external thermo-convective perturbation on cool flame dynamics
study: Simulations using FLEX flight data to explain how heating and drift change cool-flame ignition, oscillation and extinction.
earthRelevance: Low-temperature combustion knowledge for engine knock, efficiency and emissions, with validated CFD tools.

title: Cool flame transitions at radiation and stretch extinction using counterflow flames
study: Ground experiments and simulations, starting from FLEX data, mapping when hot flames turn into cool or warm flames.
earthRelevance: Cool and warm flame regions widen at higher pressure, which matters because many engines run at 20 to 40 atm.

title: Cool Flames Investigation with Gases
study: Conditions under which cool diffusion flames of propane, butane and pentane exist on a spherical burner, with CFD support.
earthRelevance: Tests cool-flame chemistry needed for ultra-lean engines; the record says efficiency could rise from 38% or lower toward 60%.

title: Pb-Sn and Pb-free solders made in terrestrial vs microgravity conditions
study: Solder joint structure and strength when made in orbit versus on Earth. A materials study, not a flame study.
earthRelevance: No combustion application. Included because it appeared in the repository search.
